[3] The primary diagnosis is osteoarthrosis, unspecified whether generalized or localized, shoulder region.
[4] Active diagnoses include osteoarthrosis, unspecified whether generalized or localized, shoulder region; diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled; unspecified vitamin D deficiency; latent syphilis, unspecified; disorders of bursae and tendons in shoulder region, unspecified; bicipital tenosynovitis; unspecified viral hepatitis C without hepatic coma; unspecified essential hypertension; esophageal reflux; and other specified complications of procedures not elsewhere classified.

[6] The patient underwent a reverse total shoulder replacement.
[7] Medications administered include influenza vaccine quadrivalent 0.5mL IM, insulin 10UNIT SC, acetaminophen 325-650mg PO/NG, morphine sulfate 1-4mg IV, metoprolol tartrate 25mg PO/NG, tacrolimus 1mg PO, aspirin 325mg PO/NG, dextrose 50% 12.5gm IV, oxycodone (immediate release) 5-10mg PO/NG, senna 8.6mg PO/NG, docusate sodium 100mg PO/NG, iso-osmotic dextrose 50mL IV, cefazolin 2g IV, 0.45% sodium chloride 1000mL IV, glucose gel 15g PO, glucagon 1mg IM, amlodipine 5mg PO/NG, hydromorphone (dilaudid) 0.12mg IVPCA, prednisone 5mg PO, sodium chloride 0.9% 1000mL IV, sodium chloride 0.9% flush 3mL IV, morphine sr (ms contin) 15mg PO, and pantoprazole 40mg PO.
[8] No microbiology results were obtained.
